title.en: Use arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment and conditional operators

say.en: 7 divided by 2 in Java is 3, not 3.5. And minus 7 percent 3 is minus 1. Knowing exactly how Java evaluates an expression is half of every ISC output question. In this lesson: Use arithmetic, relational, logical, assignment and conditional operators.
Apply precedence and associativity.
Trace prefix and postfix increment.

body.en: Arithmetic: + − * / % (on two ints, / is integer division and % gives the remainder, whose sign follows the dividend). Relational: < > <= >= == != give boolean results. Logical: && (and), || (or), ! (not); && and || are short-circuit: the right side is not evaluated if the left side already decides. Assignment: =, +=, −=, *=, /=, %=. Increment and decrement: ++ and −−. Ternary: condition ? a : b.

title.en: On the board: prefix and postfix

say.en: Prefix: change first, then use.

text.en: int a = 5;  int b = ++a;   // a = 6, b = 6

say.en: Postfix: use first, then change.

text.en: int a = 5;  int b = a++;   // a = 6, b = 5

say.en: A classic ISC trace: evaluate left to right, updating a as you go.

body.en: In a mixed expression Java promotes the smaller type to the larger before computing: int with double gives double, and byte, short and char are promoted to int in any arithmetic. So 5 / 2 is 2 but 5 / 2.0 is 2.5, and char + int is an int ('A' + 1 is 66). The + operator joins strings: "Sum " + 2 + 3 gives "Sum 23", but "Sum " + (2 + 3) gives "Sum 5", because + is evaluated left to right.

problem.en: Evaluate: int x = 10, y = 4; boolean r = x % y == 2 && ++y > 5 || x / y < 3; and give the final values.

steps.en: x % y = 2, so x % y == 2 is true.
&& now evaluates ++y > 5: y becomes 5, and 5 > 5 is false. true && false = false.
|| evaluates x / y < 3 with y = 5: 10 / 5 = 2, and 2 < 3 is true.

narration.en: Evaluate: int x = 10, y = 4; boolean r = x % y == 2 && ++y > 5 || x / y < 3; and give the final values.

say.en: Evaluate: int x equals 10, y equals 4; boolean r equals x % y == 2 && plus plus y is greater than 5 || x divided by y is less than 3; and give the final values.
x % y equals 2, so x % y == 2 is true.
&& now evaluates plus plus y is greater than 5: y becomes 5, and 5 is greater than 5 is false. true && false equals false.
|| evaluates x divided by y is less than 3 with y equals 5: 10 divided by 5 equals 2, and 2 is less than 3 is true.
false || true equals true.
So the answer is r equals true, x equals 10, y equals 5.
